Priorities as a partial order on the metrics

\(x \preceq_{\mathcal{M}, P} y\) if every loss of \(x\) has a gain above it:
\(\textcolor{dpred}{m(x) \not\preceq m(y)} \implies \exists\, m' \succ_P m,\ \textcolor{dpgreen}{m'(x) \prec m'(y)}\)

• \(P\) with no strict pairs: Pareto optimality
  • \(P\) a total order: lexicographic optimality

the landings of the last example on glide cone,

the four landings form no convex set, and the union still gives \(\mathcal{X}^*\) here

• layered extension of \(P\): layers with \(P \subseteq P_{\mathcal{B}}\), minimal when each layer has a metric below one of the layer before
  • each \(\mathcal{X}^*_{\mathcal{B}} \subseteq \mathcal{X}^*\), and one extension alone can give less, as \(\mathcal{X}^*_{\mathcal{B}^1} = \{c\}\)
  • without convexity, an optimal decision can lie in no \(\textcolor{dpred}{\mathcal{X}^*_{\mathcal{B}}}\)

Let \(\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, and let every metric be convex.
Then \(\operatorname{Min}(\mathcal{X}, {\preceq_{\mathcal{M}, P}}) = \bigcup \{\mathcal{X}^*_{\mathcal{B}} \mid \mathcal{B} \text{ a minimal layered extension of } P\}\).
A union over a family that misses a minimal one is smaller on some convex problem.

a metric may lie in several chains

\(x \preceq_{\mathcal{C}} y\) if \(x\) is lexicographically at most \(y\)
along every chain: \(\forall i,\ x \preceq_{C_i} y\)

• within a chain: the first difference from the top
    decides, so missing the target does not count
  • across chains: Pareto, so \(x \prec_{\mathcal{C}} y\) needs every chain
